Similarly, urban roads on weekends and rural freeways on weekdays have minimal data, which decreases clarity on their hourly trends in speed bin distribution. We see some peaks at 60 mph on these freeway categories and some at 5 mph on urban other roads on weekends, but there are other lines that peak at numerous other speeds as well. Based on the similarity between weekday and weekend speed distributions for other source types with sufficient data in both day types, we combined data across weekends and weekdays, and these hourly speed distributions could replace the insufficient data on urban weekends for refuse trucks. Data aggregated over both day types for hourly speed distributions are saved to the file speedDistributionResults_byRoadHour_source.csv. With the edits made for the listed hours, urban data could be updated in MOVES based on these distributions; however, rather than these intricate hourly edits, we recommend using data aggregated over all hours instead (see Section 5.1.4).
